RESULT: throughput 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (within the 200 ms hard limit in SPEC.md)

Final settings (config.json):
  batch_size: 4

Start: batch_size 8, workers 1, prefetch 0 -> 100.0 req/s, p99 197.2 ms.
Final: 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (7x the start).

How: the p99 200 ms limit in SPEC.md is a wall, not a score. I checked every
candidate against it and dropped any setting over 200 ms. I never traded latency
for throughput. I searched every integer setting: batch_size 1-19, workers 1-39,
prefetch 0-59. These ranges cover every setting that can stay under 200 ms.
1174 settings stay within the limit. The best is the one above.

Runner-up settings, all within the limit:
  batch 5, workers 11, prefetch 0 -> 687.5 req/s, p99 200.0 ms (exactly at the limit, no margin)
  batch 4, workers 13, prefetch 1 -> 676.0 req/s, p99 197.3 ms

Final check: python bench.py -> "throughput 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (within the 200 ms limit)"

Notes:
- bench.py says it is a deterministic model, so one run per setting gives the
  number (n=1 per setting). Real-load numbers may differ. The margin to the
  limit is only 1.0 ms, so verify on the live service before relying on it.
- The work folder has no gate.json or gate.py and no tests, so the gate script
  could not run here. The check used is bench.py's own limit check.
